def: Evolutionary search whose candidates are programs stored as trees, varied by swapping and regrowing branches.
The operations a genetic programming tree may use at its internal nodes, such as add, subtract and max.
The leaves a genetic programming tree may use: the program's inputs and its constants.
The guarantee that any function can accept the output of any other, so every tree built from the sets is a valid program.
Making a child by replacing a random subtree of one parent with a random subtree of another.
Growth in program size over generations without any gain in fitness, usually from useless padding that shields good code from crossover.
A penalty on program size added to the score, so that padding is not free.
Using evolutionary search, instead of gradients, to find the weights, the structure, or both, of a neural network.
NeuroEvolution of Augmenting Topologies: an algorithm that evolves network structure and weights together, starting from the smallest network.
A global, ever-increasing label given to each new connection in NEAT, so that genes can be aligned across genomes.
Grouping genomes by structural similarity and having them compete mostly within their group, to protect new structure while it is still weak.
Covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy: a method for real-valued search that learns the size and shape of its sampling cloud from ranked samples.
A square table of the variances of each parameter and how pairs of parameters vary together, which sets the shape of a Gaussian cloud.
A running sum of recent mean movements with older ones fading, used to tell steady progress from zig-zagging.
The ratio of the steepest to the gentlest curvature of a function, large for narrow valleys that are hard to search.
